SEBI Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey | CAS Update

CAS Outlook
- CAS is here to stay.
- CAS is a major structural reform.
- Initial implementation has some teething problems.
- Issues will be reviewed and addressed.
- Too early to assess participant response.

Tracking Error
- No concerns around CAS tracking error.

Market Participation

BSE CLEARING LAUNCHES 3-DAY SECURITIES LENDING & BORROWING CONTRACTS

📊 BSE Clearing introduces 3-working-day contracts in the Securities Lending & Borrowing (SLB) segment, effective August 17, 2026.

⏱️ Contracts will have a T+1 first leg and T+3 reverse leg, excluding settlement holidays.

📈 Initially, the shorter-tenor contracts will be available for F&O securities under the “D” series.

🔄 Shorter tenure provides greater flexibility for short-term securities borrowing and delivery requirements.

⚡ The facility could also support inter-exchange arbitrage and better price alignment across trading venues.

🎯 BSE Clearing expects the initiative to improve market efficiency and deepen participation in the SLB ecosystem.

🟢 Impact: Positive — shorter-tenor SLB contracts could boost flexibility, trading activity and participation on BSE’s securities lending platform.

SAFE ENTERPRISES: ENTERS HOME FURNISHINGS WITH EVOLV; SECURES FIRST COMMERCIAL ORDERS

🏠 Safe Enterprises Retail Fixtures (SERFL) is diversifying beyond retail fixtures into the home furnishings & home-living market through its new EVOLV modular platform.

🟢 Impact: Positive — Diversification expands SERFL’s addressable market and creates an additional growth engine while leveraging existing capabilities, though EVOLV is still at an early commercial stage.

BALU FORGE: SECURES MULTI-MONTH ORDER FOR 155MM EXTENDED-RANGE ARTILLERY SHELLS

🛡️ Successfully commercialised and received its first purchase order from an Indian ammunition player for 155mm ERFB BB/BT shells.

📦 Initial pilot supply of 10,000 units, following which monthly supplies at mutually agreed quantities will commence.

🎯 ERFB BB shells can extend the range of 155mm artillery to around 48 km, compared with ~38 km for systems such as the 45-calibre Dhanush.

⚙️ Order validates Balu Forge’s advanced forging & machining capabilities and strengthens its position in the defence supply chain.

🏭 Company has already commercialised standard 152mm & 155mm M107 projectiles at its automated Belgaum facility and is now moving toward more sophisticated long-range ammunition.

🌍 Management sees potential from both Indian defence requirements and global markets, as the shells meet standard NATO specifications and are compatible with key artillery platforms.

🟢 Impact: Positive — First order followed by recurring monthly supplies opens a new defence revenue stream and supports Balu Forge’s strategy of moving into higher-value, technologically advanced products.

reports.text: Dhoot Transmission

DHOOT TRANSMISSION | BUSINESS & IPO RESEARCH

Company Overview
- Electrical & Electronics supplier to auto OEMs.
- Core product: automotive wiring harnesses.
- Harnesses carry power and data signals.
- Also manufactures battery packs and sensors.
- Makes switches and electronic controllers.
- 22 manufacturing plants across India and overseas.
- 4 additional plants under construction.

Market Position
- Among India's top 2 wiring harness players.
- 2W/3W harness market share: 44.64%.
- Electric 2W/3W harness share: 70%+.
- Strong leadership in electric vehicle wiring.
- EV transition strengthens its competitive position.

Revenue Mix
- Wiring Harnesses: 77.15% of revenue.
- Battery Packs & Electronics: 22.85%.
- Direct B2B supply to OEMs.
- Embedded within OEM vehicle designs.
- Model programs typically last 5–7 years.
- Long model cycles provide revenue visibility.

Customer Base
- Bajaj Auto: 32.33% of revenue.
- TVS Motor: 19.47%.
- Honda Motorcycle India: 10.58%.
- Royal Enfield: 4.86%.
- Top 10 customers: 82.10% of revenue.
- Top 5 relationships span 6–22 years.
- Long relationships create customer stickiness.

Financial Growth
- FY23 Revenue: ₹2,126 Cr.
- FY24 Revenue: ₹2,798 Cr.
- FY25 Revenue: ₹3,445 Cr.
- FY23–25 Revenue CAGR: ~27%.
- 9M FY26 Revenue: ₹3,248 Cr.
- Annualised FY26 revenue: ~₹4,330 Cr.
- Total assets doubled since FY23.
- Growth trajectory remains strong.

Balance Sheet
- Total Equity: ₹1,309 Cr.
- Total Borrowings: ~₹822 Cr.
- Debt-to-Equity: ~0.63x.
- Trade Receivables: ₹699 Cr.
- Receivables equal ~78 days of sales.
- Business remains working-capital intensive.
- IPO proceeds can reduce leverage.

IPO Structure
- Total IPO Size: ₹3,067 Cr.
- Fresh Issue: ₹1,400 Cr.
- Offer for Sale: ~₹1,667 Cr.
- Fresh issue primarily supports deleveraging.
- OFS provides shareholder monetisation.
- Fresh issue is ~45% of IPO.
- OFS accounts for ~55%.

Use of Fresh Issue
- Repayment of company borrowings.
- Subsidiary debt repayment support.
- New plant at Jhajjar, Haryana.
- New plant at Hosur, Tamil Nadu.
- Inorganic growth opportunities.
- General corporate purposes.

EV Growth Driver
- EV kit value is 1.5–2.5x ICE.
- Higher content increases revenue per vehicle.
- Electric 2W penetration currently ~6.4%.
- EV penetration could reach 20–25% by FY31.
- Dhoot has 70%+ EV harness share.
- EV transition provides strong structural opportunity.

ICE + EV Advantage
- ~95% portfolio is EV-focused or neutral.
- EV growth directly supports content expansion.
- ICE vehicles continue generating revenue.
- Powertrain-neutral products reduce technology risk.
- Dhoot can benefit across drivetrain transitions.

Premiumisation
- 150cc+ motorcycles growing 6–9% CAGR.
- Mass segment growing 4–6% CAGR.
- Premium vehicles require higher electronic content.
- Higher content supports revenue growth.
- Premiumisation complements EV growth.

Competitive Advantages
- Strong position in 2W/3W harnesses.
- 70%+ electric segment market share.
- Deep OEM relationships.
- Long vehicle-program lifecycles.
- Embedded position in OEM designs.
- High switching costs after platform selection.
- Expanding manufacturing footprint.

Key Growth Drivers
- Rapid EV adoption.
- Higher EV content per vehicle.
- Premium motorcycle growth.
- New manufacturing capacity.
- Increasing electronics content.
- OEM platform wins.
- Potential inorganic expansion.
- Balance-sheet deleveraging.

Key Risks
- Bajaj Auto contributes 32.33% revenue.
- High dependence on top customers.
- Top 10 customers contribute 82.10%.
- Customer concentration remains major risk.
- Auto industry remains cyclical.
- Working capital intensity is high.
- Receivables remain elevated.
- IPO OFS does not add capital.
- Execution of new plants remains important.

Bull Case
- 70%+ EV harness market share.
- Strong EV structural growth.
- 27% historical revenue CAGR.
- Long-term OEM relationships.
- Higher EV content per vehicle.
- New capacity supports expansion.
- IPO proceeds reduce leverage.
- Premiumisation adds further growth.

Bear Case
- High Bajaj Auto dependence.
- 82% revenue from top 10 customers.
- Auto-sector cyclicality.
- Working-capital intensive model.
- Execution risks from rapid expansion.
- Customer concentration can amplify volatility.

Key Monitorables
- EV 2W/3W penetration.
- EV harness market share.
- Bajaj Auto revenue contribution.
- New plant commissioning.
- New OEM wins.
- Revenue per vehicle.
- Receivable days.
- Working-capital intensity.
- Debt reduction after IPO.
- Margin expansion.

Investment View
Dhoot Transmission offers a direct play on India's automotive electrification and increasing vehicle electronics content. Its strongest differentiator is the 70%+ market share in electric 2W/3W wiring harnesses, combined with long OEM relationships and a largely EV-focused or powertrain-neutral portfolio.

The biggest issue is customer concentration, particularly the 32.33% dependence on Bajaj Auto. Therefore, future growth should ideally come alongside greater customer diversification.

Key Takeaway
- Dhoot Transmission is a strong EV supply-chain play with leadership in electric 2W/3W wiring harnesses, 27% FY23–25 revenue CAGR and long-standing OEM relationships. The ₹1,400 Cr fresh IPO proceeds should support deleveraging and new capacity, while rising EV penetration and higher content per vehicle provide structural growth. However, high customer concentration, working-capital intensity and auto-sector cyclicality remain the key risks to monitor.

Tukaram Mundhe's FDA Cracks Down on Goregaon Film City, AICWA Demands State-Wide Inspections

IAS Tukaram Mundhe-led FDA has suspended the license of a canteen in Goregaon Film City after unhygienic conditions were found upon crackdown, according to a post by All Indian Cine Workers Association on X. 

The move follows appeals by the AICWA  to conduct surprise checks and inspections over concerns of the quality of food and water in film sets and studios across Mumbai. 

"We are grateful to the Maharashtra FDA team, under the leadership of Hon'ble Commissioner Shri Tukaram Mundhe, IAS, for taking prompt action on the demand raised by the All Indian Cine Workers Association," the post stated. 

It added that, upon AICWA's demand, the Maharashtra FDA team conducted an inspection at a canteen in Goregaon Film City, Mumbai, where unhygienic conditions were found. The canteen's licence was subsequently suspended.

AI Data Centre Value chain | India Picks & Shovels Map

1. Compute Engine
- Netweb Technologies: AI GPU servers.
- E2E Networks: GPU cloud infrastructure.
- Orient Technologies: GPU and cloud infrastructure.
- Panache Digilife: AI servers and hardware.
- Netweb AI systems: ~62% of Q1FY27 revenue.

2. Electrical Infrastructure
- Marine Electricals: MV/LV panels.
- Vivid Electromech: PDU and panels.
- RMC Switchgears: DC control panels.
- Schneider Electric Infrastructure: switchgear and distribution.
- Marine receives repeat data-centre orders.
- Vivid: ~50% FY26 revenue from data centres.

3. Cables & Fibre
- APAR Industries: LV/MV DC cables.
- Polycab: power, control and fibre cables.
- KEI Industries: LV/MV/EHV cables.
- RR Kabel: power and fire-safe cables.
- HFCL: AI data-centre connectivity.
- Sterlite Technologies: high-density fibre.
- APAR approved for major US DC projects.
- HFCL investing ₹215 Cr in connectivity.

4. Grid & Transformers
- Hitachi Energy India: transformers and GIS.
- GE Vernova T&D: transformers and grid equipment.
- Shilchar Technologies: customised transformers.
- CG Power: transformers and switchgear.
- Voltamp Transformers: transformers.
- AI expansion requires substantial grid infrastructure.
- More AI means higher power demand.
- Higher power demand drives transformer demand.

5. Cooling & Thermal Management
- KRN Heat Exchanger: cooling systems.
- Aeroflex Industries: liquid-cooling systems.
- Thermax: cooling and thermal infrastructure.
- Blue Star: chillers and precision cooling.
- Amber Enterprises: HVAC ecosystem.
- United Heat Exchanger: DC cooling.
- Aeroflex started AI/DC liquid-cooling dispatches.
- Thermax disclosed ₹400+ Cr US DC order.
- Higher GPU density increases cooling demand.

6. Water Infrastructure
- Ion Exchange: water treatment and reuse.
- Thermax: water and cooling infrastructure.
- VA Tech Wabag: high-purity water systems.
- Effwa Infra: emerging DC water opportunity.
- Cooling increases water-management requirements.
- Water recycling can reduce resource intensity.
- Thermal management remains closely linked.

7. Backup Power
- Powerica: large DG systems.
- Prostarm Info Systems: UPS and batteries.
- Cummins India: standby generation.
- Kirloskar Oil Engines: DG systems.
- Amara Raja: industrial and UPS batteries.
- Exide Industries: backup batteries.
- Hyperscale data centres require high reliability.
- UPS and batteries protect against outages.
- DG systems provide extended backup.

AI Data Centre Value Chain
- AI GPUs drive compute demand.
- Compute requires reliable electricity.
- Electricity requires transformers and switchgear.
- Power distribution requires cables and PDUs.
- GPUs generate substantial heat.
- Cooling systems manage thermal loads.
- Cooling requires water infrastructure.
- Backup systems protect against outages.

Key Themes
- AI expansion drives data-centre capacity.
- Data-centre capacity drives power demand.
- Power demand drives grid investment.
- GPU density drives cooling demand.
- Reliability drives backup-power investment.
- Water efficiency becomes increasingly important.

Key Monitorables
- Data-centre capacity additions.
- AI GPU deployments.
- Transformer order books.
- Cable demand growth.
- Cooling-system orders.
- Liquid-cooling adoption.
- UPS and battery demand.
- Data-centre power requirements.
- Water-treatment opportunities.

Key Takeaway
- The AI data-centre opportunity extends far beyond GPUs and semiconductors. India's AI infrastructure build-out can create a broad picks-and-shovels opportunity across transformers, switchgear, cables, fibre, cooling, water treatment, UPS, batteries and backup power. As AI workloads increase power density, the companies supplying the physical infrastructure required to build and operate data centres could become important beneficiaries of the AI capex cycle.

TD Power Systems Limited ("TDPS") has entered
into a Build-to-Print Manufacturing Framework Agreement dated August 13, 2026 with Siemens
Energy, Inc. ("Siemens Energy"), pursuant to which TDPS will manufacture and supply 2-pole
Generators in accordance with Siemens Energy's designs, drawings and specifications.

In simple words

TD Power has signed a 10 year deal with Siemens Energy's US arm to build large 2-pole generators for Siemens.

Siemens gives the designs and drawings, TDPS manufactures them. Siemens is doing this because its own factories are full (the AI data-centre power boom has its order books stuffed for years), so it needs someone qualified to make machines on its behalf. 

TDPS has licensed Siemens' 2-pole technology for over a decade, so this is that relationship getting upgraded from "we borrow your design" to "we are your factory."

Business only comes through individual purchase orders whenever Siemens issues them. So nothing goes into the order book today, and since these machines take 18–20 months to build, real revenue starts showing up around FY29. 

Also, since TDPS is building to Siemens' design and not its own, it doesn't own the technology and likely earns a thinner margin per unit  but with far higher volume, less design risk and better factory utilisation. 

Think of it as TDPS becoming a "CDMO for generators" for one of the world's top three turbine makers: strategically a very strong position, but for now it's a licence to receive orders, not the orders themselves.

NOMURA ON TATA MOTORS PV

Rating: Neutral
Target: ₹389

• India PV: Strong demand, but steep cost pressure

• JLR: Success of new launches remains key monitorable

• China outlook challenging, while US market offers growth opportunity

• Valuation at 3.8x FY28F EV/EBITDA seen as reasonable considering risks

• Upside: Higher India PV volumes and successful JLR launches

• Downside: Weaker JLR margins, negative FCF and near-term India PV margin pressure

HSBC ON TATA MOTORS PV

Rating: Hold
Target: ₹360

• Domestic demand momentum strong, but margin hit from commodity costs

• Commodity headwinds likely to continue in Q2

• JLR structural recovery depends on new model launches as existing portfolio has aged

• Estimates cut due to higher commodity and operating costs

CLSA ON TATA MOTORS PV

Rating: Outperform
Target: ₹452

• JLR EBIT margin at 2.8% in Q1FY27, 90 bps above estimates

• Domestic PV EBITDA margin at 4.3%, 250 bps below estimates

• JLR FCF outflow at £1.0 bn; management retains FY27 guidance of ~4% EBIT margin and breakeven FCF

• Upcoming launches, North America focus and cost reduction to support JLR

• Domestic PV demand outlook remains strong

• Dealer inventory at ~30 days; dispatches guided at 65k–70k units/month ahead of festive season

CITI ON TATA MOTORS PV

Rating: Sell
Target: ₹305

• Q1 significantly below expectations for JLR and India PV due to severe cost headwinds

• India demand outlook remains positive; FY27 volume growth guidance at high double-digits

• 2Q margins expected to remain similar to Q1 due to rising commodity costs

• JLR reiterates double-digit FY27 revenue growth guidance; cost efficiencies and higher ASPs to support margins

• Focus remains on four upcoming new launches

• Citi remains concerned about margin trajectory, especially in India PV where EBIT remains negative despite healthy volumes and PLI benefits

HSBC ON MAX FIN

Rating: Buy
Target: ₹2,100

• Q1FY27 APE growth broadly in line with estimates

• Stronger-than-expected margin uplift drove VNB beat

• Distribution and product diversification expected to support sustainable medium-term growth

Rating: Accumulate
Target: ₹670 vs ₹650 earlier

• Domino’s remains steady; Popeyes emerging as second growth engine

• Strategic initiatives continue to drive positive LFL growth

• Jubilant Food is Citi’s preferred pick in QSR coverage

MACQUARIE ON TATA MOTORS PV

Rating: Outperform
Target: ₹381

• Margins disappoint; near-term risks persist

• India margins disappoint; JLR in line with muted expectations

• Positive on domestic growth outlook

• Margin risks remain a key concern

Magellanic Cloud Limited’s Wholly Owned Subsidiary Provigil Surveillance Limited Receives ₹3.73 Cr LOA from PSU Major DFCCIL

• Order Value: ₹3.73 Cr from Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited (DFCCIL).

• Scope: Supply, Installation, Testing & Commissioning (SITC) and Operations & Maintenance (O&M) of an E-Surveillance System across a section of the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor (WDFC).

• Tenure: 5-year contract on an OPEX model.

• Key Scope: E-surveillance for theft prevention, remote monitoring, asset & facility protection, perimeter security, dock management and Command & Control Centre services.

• Project Location: Kishangarh Balawas – New Rewari – New Phulera – New Kishangarh – Madar section of WDFC.

KRN Heat Exchanger and Refrigeration Limited Delivers Triple-Digit Growth in Q1 FY27

📌Q1 FY27 Consolidated Key Financial Highlights
- Revenue from Operations of ₹252.32 Cr, YoY growth of 118.87%
- EBITDA of ₹49.06 Cr, YoY growth of 178.85%
- EBITDA Margin of 19.44%, up 418 bps YoY
- Net Profit of ₹32.90 Cr, YoY growth of 164.84%
- Net Profit Margin of 13.04%, up 266 bps YoY

📌Q1 FY27 Standalone Key Financial Highlights
- Revenue from Operations of ₹181.97 Cr, YoY growth of 59.07%
- EBITDA of ₹24.67 Cr, YoY growth of 24.67%
- Net Profit of ₹18.67 Cr, YoY growth of 19.02%

📌Key Business Highlights
- Overseas revenue grew 177.31% YoY to ₹52.38 Cr, with exports contributing 20.76% of segment revenue
- Domestic revenue stood at ₹199.94 Cr, up 107.42% YoY
- Exports were spread across 14 countries, with the USA, France, Vietnam, UAE and Italy among the key markets
- ₹350 Cr QIP completed during the quarter, with net proceeds of ₹341.79 Cr. The funds raised have been allocated towards the stated objective

RECODE STUDIOS OPENS FIRST MODERN TRADE STORE; PLANS 15–20 MORE IN FY27 🚀

• 🏬 Opened its first NewU store at The Opulent Mall, Ghaziabad.

• 🤝 Partnership with NewU, the beauty & personal care retail chain operated by H&B Stores, a Dabur India subsidiary.

• 📈 Targets 15–20 additional NewU stores over the next 12 months across high-potential markets.

• 💎 Expansion aims to strengthen presence in premium & luxury beauty products and organised retail.

• 🎯 Management expects the network expansion to improve brand visibility, margins and average order values.

reiterating its target of 200-250 annual store additions; and

multiple margin levers make it confident of managing near-term input cost pressures

MACQUARIE ON LENSKART

Target ₹675

Earlier Target ₹625

Recommendation Outperform

KEY TAKEAWAYS

Q1: India in line, international beat

In-line India performance supplemented by stronger international margin expansion

Like strong volume growth, ongoing premiumisation (lenses/frames), attractive Rs 500 entry-level offering, and potential for 10k+ stores in India

Stronger international margins drive a 4% EPS upgrade and 8% TP increase

MOSL ON HAL

MOSL maintains Buy with target price at ₹5,800 vs ₹5,500

HAL reported healthy Q1FY27 numbers with margins ahead of estimates to

HAL has ramped up LCA manufacturing capacity to 24 aircraft annually

Tejas deliveries are expected to ramp up from FY28

LCH Prachand, ALFP31 engines, HTT-40, RD-33 engines and Su-30 aircraft are expected to support growth

MOSL expects revenue, EBITDA and PAT CAGR of 23%, 19% and 17% over FY26-29

JEFFERIES ON BANKS

KEY TAKEAWAYS

RBI Proposes Draft Norms to Harmonize Interest Rate Policy Across Lenders

Requires lending rates to be set per transparent structure linked to benchmark & a positive spread

PLR and spread components can be set per internal policies

Benchmark reset frequency cap at 3 months for floating rate loans can improve transmission

Restricting repricing of spread components may reduce pricing flexibility

NBFCs are not required to move to EBLR framework like banks

JEFFERIES ON GRASIM

Target ₹3910

Earlier Target ₹3600

Recommendation Accumulate

KEY TAKEAWAYS

Standalone Business Momentum Accelerates

Sharp Q1 beat, with all segments outperforming

VSF & Chemicals rebounded on pricing tailwinds, while new biz continue to scale

Paints guiding for 50% YoY growth in FY27 & FY28 targets intact

B2B e-commerce is set to turn profitable by FY27-end

MACQUARIE ON APOLLO HOSPITAL

Target ₹6230

Recommendation Underperform

KEY TAKEAWAYS

Q1 - all round beat

Operational beat driven by revenue

MACQUARIE ON PAINTS

KEY TAKEAWAYS

Read-through from Grasim's Q1 call

Part of price hike benefits to flow into Q2 sales

Share of premium and luxury products steady at 65%

Prefer Asian Paints in the sector

JEFFERIES ON LENSKART

Target ₹680

Earlier Target ₹600

Recommendation Accumulate

KEY TAKEAWAYS

Authenticity Matters More Than Legacy

Q1 continues to build the story, with strong growth & sharp margin expansion

Market creation remains a top priority, with supply, rather than demand, being a key constraint in India

Company now plays at the bottom end with a fully loaded Rs 500 product, while a clear premiumization trend is visible

Margin improvement in international should put a key investor concern to rest

MORGAN STANLEY ON FINANCIAL

KEY TAKEAWAYS

RBI's draft guidelines on interest rates on loans and advances

Think that PSU banks have a much higher proportion of MCLR based loans, relative to private banks

PSU Banks would need to rejig their pricing models

Given the significant transition time, see the impact on financials as contained and gradual, if any

CITI ON APOLLO HOSPITAL

Target ₹10770

Recommendation Accumulate

KEY TAKEAWAYS

Q1: Strong Execution Across Businesses, Hospitals EBITDA up 25% like for like

Despite the expansions, ROCE continues to remain strong at 28.5%

Company announced four new hospitals and now targets >5,800 beds addition over the next five years

Provides strong visibility on medium-term earnings growth

Apollo remains top India hospitals pick

CITI ON ASTRAL

Target ₹1900

Recommendation Accumulate

KEY TAKEAWAYS

Outperformance on Volumes in a Challenging Quarter

Plumbing volumes were impacted by volatility in PVC prices in Q1

They have sharply recovered in July

See double-digit volume growth in the first 4.5 months of FY27

Mgmt remains confident of achieving their guidance for 10-15% volume growth

MACQUARIE ON GMR AIRPORTS

Target ₹125

Recommendation Outperform

KEY TAKEAWAYS

Temporary traffic headwinds, structural story intact

Continue to see value creation shifting beyond traffic growth

Toward higher aero yields, non-aero monetisation and airport adjacencies

Near term focus remains on Hyderabad traffic recovery, Bhogapuram ramp-up, Nagpur integration and progress on real estate monetization
